title: t18819: fix(pulse): exact-head approval supersedes a worker's self-applied draft hold-for-review
body:
## Task


A worker draft checkpoint whose own runner applied `hold-for-review` can never continue, even after the brief owner supplies the requested input and posts a valid exact-head `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` envelope. Make a trusted exact-head approval supersede a hold that the approved runner applied to its own draft, and stop headless workers from applying that hold in the first place.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

A worker draft checkpoint whose own runner applied `hold-for-review` can never continue, even after the brief owner supplies the requested input and posts a valid exact-head `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` envelope. Make a trusted exact-head approval supersede a hold that the approved runner applied to its own draft, and stop headless workers from applying that hold in the first place.

## Why (evidence)

- Issue #36061 / draft PR #36070: the worker exited `Terminal blocker: reason=input_required owner=maintainer` (10:43:49Z) and, in the same run, its runner applied `hold-for-review` to its own draft (PR label event 10:43:00Z, actor = PR author). The issue-side blocker re-armed (15:30Z) and the owner posted the evidence contract plus exact-head approval comment 6533310594 (20:57Z).
- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh has-open-pr 36061` → "draft PR #36070 is a durable checkpoint; ordinary redispatch is blocked", while `_pr_checkpoint_revised_target` keeps every real PR label, so `_pr_checkpoint_pr_metadata_is_eligible` rejects the protected draft. Neither ordinary dispatch nor approved continuation can proceed: a permanent stall; the dirty-PR sweep only escalates `hold-for-review-label` to a maintainer.
- Same shape on another managed repo's worker draft (hold applied by the PR author's runner on 2026-10-28).
- Source of the self-hold: `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md` outcome C ("apply `hold-for-review` and stop") has no release path once the decision is supplied, and duplicates the structured `input_required` terminal blocker whose recovery re-arms automatically.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh` — in `_pr_checkpoint_revised_target`, after the approval validates, treat `hold-for-review` on the PR as superseded only when ALL hold: every `labeled hold-for-review` event on the PR was by the PR author (= approved runner), the newest such event precedes the approval comment, the issue body has no PR-only completion contract marker, the issue has no feedback-route automation-hold record for that PR, and the PR has no `release-approval-required` label. Strip only that label from the local normalized view; every other protective label stays enforced. Fail closed on unreadable events.
2. `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — `_pcc_target_row` reports whether the approved target carried a superseded hold; `_pcc_dispatch` removes the PR `hold-for-review` label after a successful exact-head dispatch so the finished PR can merge.
3. `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md` outcome C — headless workers post the decision comment and exit through the structured `BLOCKED` input-required terminal blocker; never label their own PR `hold-for-review`.

## Acceptance

- A valid exact-head approval newer than a runner-self-applied PR `hold-for-review` routes the draft to continuation; the label is removed after dispatch.
- A hold applied by any other actor, applied after the approval, on a PR-only-contract issue, with a feedback-route automation-hold record, or with `release-approval-required` still rejects the target.
- Existing checkpoint tests pass: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-claim-helper.sh`; ShellCheck clean.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`

</details>

title: fix: generation enrollment refuses group-writable git admin dirs (umask 002), failing most fresh precreations
body:
## What

Since GH#35996 (worktree generation enrollment, merged 2026-10-30), `worktree-helper.sh add` exits 1 after `git worktree add` succeeds on hosts whose umask is `002`. Pulse logs this as `worktree_precreation_failed` and drops the dispatch; the ceremony before precreation (about 80 s per attempt) is wasted, and the retained worktree is left behind.

## Reproducer

1. On Linux with `umask 002`, create a disposable repo with one commit.
2. From that repo, run `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_BASE=<seed-sha> .agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh add feature/auto-x-gh1 --issue 1`, with the registry and worktree base pointed at temp dirs.
3. Observe `Generation enrollment refused` and `Worktree retained: generation enrollment failed`, with exit 1.

## Evidence (one Linux runner, found while working on #36132)

- `dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400`: `dedup.pre_runtime_failure:worktree_precreation_failed` n=35, against `precreate.helper_add` n=49 and `precreate.helper_deps` n=15. In this window, most fresh creations fail after `create_worktree`.
- Raw records per failed attempt show `precreate.registry_register` and `precreate.create_worktree` but no `precreate.verify_generation`. The failure is therefore inside `worktree_create_registered` after registration, in `_worktree_enroll_generation` (`.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh:85`).
- Disposable reproduction: `worktree-helper.sh add` in a temp repo prints `Generation enrollment refused: {"reason": "ValueError", "status": "unavailable", ...}` followed by `Worktree retained: generation enrollment failed`, with `helper_rc=1`.
- A read-only probe of `GenerationEnrollment.has_schema_one_gap()` on a retained live worktree raises `ValueError("git-directory-must-be-owned-and-not-shared-writable")` from `_git_directory()` (`.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/enrollment.py:42`). That check rejects `st_mode & 0o022`.
- Git creates `.git/worktrees/<name>` under the process umask. On this host the directories are `775` (umask `002`, user-private groups, the Ubuntu default), so every enrollment check fails.
- `pulse.log` shows only `helper_reason: 'none'` and the first 120 characters of stdout. The refusal reason never reaches the log (`_dlw_precreate_helper_reason` matches only `managed-worktree:`, `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_LIFECYCLE_DISPOSITION=` and `Error:`).
- The pre-existing failure of `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh` ("real managed precreation compensates rejected ownership...", which also fails on `main`) is a related fixture problem: its temp `HOME` has no `.aidevops/.agent-workspace`, so `LifecycleRegistry.initialize` raises `FileNotFoundError` on the state-dir parent.

## How

1. Decide the trust rule in `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/enrollment.py` `_git_directory()`. One option: keep refusing world-writable (`0o002`), and allow group-writable only when the group is the owner's user-private group (gid matches the owner's primary group and that group has no other members). Another: tighten permissions at creation by running `chmod go-w` on the new admin dir in `worktree_create_registered` before enrollment. Keep the backlink and ownership checks either way.
2. Make the refusal reason visible: add `Generation enrollment refused:` (or the JSON `reason`) to the patterns in `_dlw_precreate_helper_reason` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`). Also have `registry.py` `main()` report the `ValueError` message for enrollment, not only `type(error).__name__`.
3. Fix the test fixture so the temp `HOME` state-dir parent exists (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh`, managed precreation block).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/enrollment.py
- EDIT: .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/registry.py
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fresh pre-creation succeeds on a host with umask `002`. Enrollment still refuses world-writable or foreign-owned git admin dirs.
- [ ] A refused enrollment logs its reason in `pulse.log`.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh` passes with 0 failures.
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests` passes.
- [ ] After deploy, `dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report 86400` shows `worktree_precreation_failed` near zero on the affected runner.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on changed scripts.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh`
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests`

Ref #35996. Found during #36132.

title: Review followup: PR #36144 — chore(release): preserve signed v3.39.98 publication
body:
## Unaddressed review bot suggestions PR #36144 was merged with unaddressed review bot feedback. Each comment below includes its file path, line number, a direct link to the inline review comment, and a `diff` fence with the code context the bot was flagging. Resolved and outdated threads are filtered out via GitHub's GraphQL review-thread state. Read the relevant lines, decide whether the suggestion is correct, and either apply the fix or close this issue with a wontfix rationale. **Source PR:** https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/36144 --- ### You are the triager (worker-is-triager rule) This issue is **auto-created from review bot output** and dispatched directly to you. Review bots can be wrong: hallucinated line refs, false premises about codebase structure, template-driven sweeps without measurements (see GH#17832-17835 for prior art and `AGENTS.md` "AI-Generated Issue Quality"). **Do not assume the bot is correct.** Verify before acting. You must end in exactly one of three outcomes — no fourth "hand it back to the human" path exists. Humans approve decisions; they do not re-do analysis. #### Outcome A — Premise falsified → close the issue 1. Read the cited `file:line` (listed under *Files to modify* below). 2. If the bot's claim is factually wrong (file doesn't exist at that line, function doesn't behave as described, "auto-generated" section isn't actually auto-generated, etc.), **close the issue** with a comment in this shape: > **Premise falsified.** \. \ actually shows, with a `file:line` citation or one-line quote\>. > Not acting. No PR. No further dispatch. The closing comment trains the next session reading this thread and the noise filter. #### Outcome B — Premise correct + fix is obvious → implement and PR 1. Verify the bot's premise as above. 2. Read the Worker Guidance section below, open a worktree, implement. 3. Open a PR with a `Resolves` closing reference in the body using THIS issue's actual number, not the source PR's, so merge auto-closes it. 4. Follow the normal Lifecycle Gate (brief, tests, review-bot-gate, merge, postflight). #### Outcome C — Premise correct but approach is a genuine judgment call Only use this path if you reach it after Outcomes A and B don't apply: the bot's finding is real, but the fix requires a decision that is architectural, policy, breaking-change, or otherwise genuinely outside what you can resolve autonomously. In that case, post a **decision comment** with exactly these fields: - **Premise check:** one line, confirming the finding is real. - **Analysis:** 2-4 bullets on the trade-offs. - **Recommended path:** the option you would take if the decision were yours, with rationale. - **Specific question:** the single decision the human needs to make (yes/no or pick-one, not open-ended). Then exit `BLOCKED` as `input_required` with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER=maintainer` and stop; the answer in this issue body re-arms dispatch. title: t18820: fix(compaction): fixed compaction effort, credential-aware routing with Haiku fallback, simple tier high
body:
## Task


Make OpenCode compaction (a) run at a fixed, sufficient reasoning effort regardless of the parent session's variant, (b) route only to providers that have usable credentials, falling back to Haiku 5.5 and then the parent model, and (c) raise the `simple` tier reasoning floor from `medium` to `high` (or `max` if replay evidence supports it).

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make OpenCode compaction (a) run at a fixed, sufficient reasoning effort regardless of the parent session's variant, (b) route only to providers that have usable credentials, falling back to Haiku 5.5 and then the parent model, and (c) raise the `simple` tier reasoning floor from `medium` to `high` (or `max` if replay evidence supports it).

## Why

- `capCompactionEffort` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-routing.mjs`) only lowers effort. OpenCode sends the parent session variant with compaction and variant options merge last, so a `low` session compacts at `low`, and the routed Luna compaction can never exceed the simple-tier `medium`.
- Local evidence: 78 Luna-medium compactions in 14 days averaged ~200 reasoning tokens for ~87K input. That is thin deliberation for a step that must preserve session aims, progress and next actions.
- `applyCompactionRouting` picks the first simple candidate whose `config.provider` limit fits. The plugin always writes `config.provider.openai.models` (GPT-6 context caps), so OpenCode lists `openai` as a `source: "config"` provider even without credentials. Without an OpenAI account, compaction is routed to `openai/gpt-6-luna` and fails with "OpenAI API key is missing" (same root cause as GH#35762, which fixed subagent routing but not config-time compaction routing).
- Haiku 5.5 (1M context) is never selected because its limit lives in the models.dev catalog, not `config.provider`; the "Haiku's 168K" comment is stale (Haiku 4.5).

## How

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-routing.mjs`: credential-aware candidate filter (auth.json key presence, known provider env keys, credential-bearing provider options, enabled/disabled providers, local providers trusted); Claude limit fallback from `model-limits.mjs` `CLAUDE_MODEL_LIMITS`; fixed compaction effort target applied both up and down, constrained to the compaction model's available variants.
- `.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json` (+ `aidevops.defaults.jsonc`, `shared-model-tier.sh` fallbacks if they carry simple reasoning): simple tier reasoning `high`; compaction effort setting.
- `.agents/tools/context/model-routing.md`: document routing, fallback order and effort.
- Tests: extend existing `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs` compaction cases.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-routing.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs`
- `.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json`
- `.agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-model-tier.sh`
- `.agents/tools/context/model-routing.md`

## Acceptance

- No OpenAI credentials + Anthropic credentials: compaction routes to `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`.
- No credentials for any simple candidate: compaction stays on the parent model.
- Compaction effort equals the configured target whether the session variant is lower or higher, never an unsupported variant.
- Replay of real compactions at medium/high/xhigh/max (Luna) and Haiku 5.5 recorded in the PR with latency, reasoning tokens and retention notes.

## Verification

`node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-routing.mjs` and the plugin test suite; replay evidence via forked sessions summarised through `opencode serve`.

</details>

title: pulse merge pass: hold PRs whose negated or contradicted closing reference would close an issue
body:
## Observed defect

A headless worker opened a partial-delivery PR in a managed application repo. The body said `For #N. Keep the issue open` and ended with `Merge records the retry evidence only and must not close #N`. GitHub's `closingIssuesReferences` listed #N because of `close #N`. Pulse's deterministic merge pass merged the PR, closed #N and applied `status:done`, closing an unfinished consolidated task.

The GH#33539 creation guard would have caught this. Running the deployed `_gh_pr_body_negated_closing_ref` (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`) on the live body matches `not close #N`. However:

- The PR was not created through `gh_create_pr`: it has no origin label and no labelling events, while every sibling PR from the same runner has `origin:worker`.
- The body's edit history shows the phrase was present at creation.
- So the only guard sits at creation, and a bypassed creation path reaches merge unchecked.

## Expected behavior

The merge pass must not let a negated or contradicted closing reference close an issue:

1. Before merging, run the GH#33539 detector on the PR body. Ignore fenced code and inline code, as the detector does.
2. Treat it as a contradiction when the body cites an issue with `For #N` or `Ref #N` but GitHub lists that issue in `closingIssuesReferences`.
3. On either signal, do not merge. Either repair the body through `gh_pr_edit_safe` (replace the negated clause with neutral prose such as `The issue remains open.` and keep `For #N`), or skip it with one log line and route it through the existing fix-worker path. Never post more than one comment per PR head.
4. Optionally, report merge candidates that lack any origin label, since that shows the creation wrappers were bypassed.

Valid leaf closure (`Resolves #N` with no contradiction) and the existing confirmed-closure reconciliation must not change.

## Scope and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`: `_check_pr_merge_gates` and `_extract_linked_issue`.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`: reuse `_gh_pr_body_negated_closing_ref`; do not duplicate the regex.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`: apply the same pre-merge check.
- Tests: extend the existing merge-pass harness pattern and `test-gh-edit-safety.sh` section 11 using synthetic fixture references.
- How the worker created a PR outside `gh_create_pr` is **unknown**. Note it if found, but the merge-time guard is the fix.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-edit-safety.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-closing-contradiction.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-issue-sync-authority.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh`

## Verification

ShellCheck zero violations on edited scripts. Run the merge-pass and edit-safety test scripts. A synthetic PR body with `For #123` plus `must not close #123` is held or repaired, never merged with a close. `Resolves #123` still merges and closes as before.

body:
## Consolidation target: #36105

**Parent issue:** #36105 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t18814: fix(sync-workflows): re-pin legacy @main loc-badge callers to release SHA and...
**Parent labels:** `bug,status:available,auto-dispatch,origin:interactive,tier:standard,consolidation-in-progress`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #36105 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #36105:**

```bash
gh issue comment 36105 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 36105 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 36105 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 36105 $NEW_NUM
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #36105 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #36105.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".

title: playwright-runtime runtime-check and setup ignore AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE and reinstall bundled Chromium
body:
## Observed

With `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE` set to an installed browser (Brave) and the bundled Chromium builds removed from the Playwright cache, `playwright-runtime.mjs browser-executable` correctly resolves the installed browser, but:

- `node ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs runtime-check` exits 1 with `"chromiumExecutable": null, "ready": false`, because `ownedRuntimeStatus()` only checks `chromium.executablePath()` of the owned prefix.
- `_setup_browser_tools_playwright` in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh` (around line 401) treats that as "not installed" and prompts, default Y, to run `playwright-runtime.mjs install chromium firefox webkit`, re-downloading the bundled Chromium the operator deliberately retired.

Bundled Playwright Chromium is pinned to an early build of each Chromium branch (Playwright 1.64.1 ships 156.0.8078.4) and lags later Chrome security releases, so an operator-configured auto-updating browser should satisfy readiness.

## Expected

When `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE` points to an existing executable, `runtime-check` reports ready (package importable + configured browser present), and setup skips the bundled browser download, or at least defaults to No and explains why.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs`: `ownedRuntimeStatus()`, `ownedChromiumExecutable()`, `runtime-check` command.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`: `_setup_browser_tools_playwright`.
- Possibly `.agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh` (uses `runtime-check`).

## Verification

1. Set `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE` to an installed Chromium-based browser and remove `chromium-*` / `chromium_headless_shell-*` from the Playwright cache.
2. `node .agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs runtime-check` exits 0 and reports the configured executable.
3. Run setup non-interactively: no `playwright-runtime.mjs install` attempted.
4. With the variable unset, behaviour is unchanged.

title: t18824: fix(pulse): recover abandoned worker-draft claims so stranded drafts are continued
body:
## Task


When a worker or continuation exits without persisting `CLAIM_RELEASED` (crash, kill, machine sleep, or a dropped release), and its issue has an open worker **draft** PR, no recovery path ever releases or continues it. The issue stays `status:in-progress` + assigned indefinitely and the draft is never finished.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When a worker or continuation exits without persisting `CLAIM_RELEASED` (crash, kill, machine sleep, or a dropped release), and its issue has an open worker **draft** PR, no recovery path ever releases or continues it. The issue stays `status:in-progress` + assigned indefinitely and the draft is never finished.

## Why

Two live examples (2026-10-31):

- #35977 / draft #35984 — assigned `marcusquinn`, `status:in-progress` since 2026-10-30T16:29Z; last push 16:37Z by a continuation that exited without release.
- #36061 / draft #36070 — approved continuation (`CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` for head `7900b24d`) launched by `vladimirdulov` at 22:44Z; `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready expires_at=1793407574` (00:46Z) expired with no terminal lease, release or PR update; still `status:in-progress` + assigned.

Every recovery path refuses them (pulse.log evidence):

1. `pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh` `_normalize_stale_open_pr_blocks_reset` — any open linked PR blocks the stale reset ("durable implementation handoff exists"), including an abandoned worker draft.
2. Layer 6 (`dispatch-dedup-stale.sh` `_recover_stale_assignment` → `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION` → `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch`) — `_pcc_dispatch` sets `PCC_CHECKPOINT_ASSIGNEE` to the issue assignee and requires it to equal the draft author, so a draft continued by a different runner is rejected (`PR_CHECKPOINT_TARGET_REJECTED: reason=pr_metadata_ineligible`, #35977). Any trusted `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` comment disables the legacy route (`pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh` `_pr_checkpoint_issue_metadata_is_eligible`), and `pr-checkpoint-revision.py` `successors_valid` rejects once the approved successor's claim is unreleased (`issue_metadata_ineligible`, #36061).
3. `dispatch-stalled` (`_pcc_dispatch_stalled`) — skips any assigned issue ("Assigned drafts belong to stale-assignment recovery (Layer 6)").
4. `pulse-draft-checkpoint-unblock.sh` — only handles `status:blocked`.

The companion fix for dropped releases (#36184: repo-state authority indeterminate → retry instead of silent skip) reduces how often this happens but cannot cover crashes, kills or sleeps.

## How

Make the stale-assignment path release a provably abandoned claim on a **worker draft** so the existing, bounded unassigned route (`dispatch-stalled`, which accepts `stale_assignment_reset` via `_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN` and has per-head/per-PR fuses) takes over:

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh` — in `_normalize_stale_open_pr_blocks_reset` / `_normalize_stale_should_skip_reset`, keep blocking for ready PRs, protected drafts and ambiguous linkage (`_stale_recovery_find_open_pr` kinds). For `draft_checkpoint`, block only while there is liveness evidence: a local continuation process (`--session-key pr-checkpoint-continuation-<owner>-<repo>-<pr>` as built by `_prrts_safe_slug`, or `issue-<N>`), a non-terminal `DISPATCH_LEASE` whose `expires_at` is in the future, or PR head/updatedAt activity newer than `WORKER_MAX_RUNTIME`. Otherwise fall through to the existing dispatch-info checks and the audited `_normalize_stale_post_release` reset (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=stale_assignment_reset`).
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-locks.sh` — `has_worker_for_repo_issue` should also recognise a live continuation session for a PR linked to the issue (so dispatch layers never treat a running continuation as absent).
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — `_pcc_dispatch`: derive the checkpoint author from the live PR `author.login` (as `_pcc_dispatch_stalled` already does) instead of assuming it equals the stale assignee; keep `expected_assignee` as the claim being replaced.
- Approved revisions (#36061 shape): after an approved successor's claim is released by `stale_assignment_reset`, make sure the next continuation is either accepted by `pr-checkpoint-revision.py` (successor released) or records one `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` comment — never silent. Do not weaken approval binding (head/ref/brief hash/24h window/trusted approver).

Reference patterns: `_pcc_dispatch_stalled` (unassigned continuation with ownership transfer), `_pcc_expired_claim_evidence` (expired-lease evidence), `_normalize_stale_post_release` (audited reset).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-locks.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-open-pr.sh`

## Acceptance

- An issue assigned to a departed worker, with an open unprotected `origin:worker` draft, no live lease/process and no PR activity within `WORKER_MAX_RUNTIME`, is released once with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=stale_assignment_reset` and then continued at the exact head by `dispatch-stalled` (or receives one attention record when the per-head/per-PR fuse is reached).
- A live continuation (local process or unexpired lease) is never reset.
- Ready PRs, protected drafts (hold/interactive/no-takeover) and ambiguous linkage still block the reset exactly as today (existing tests in `test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-open-pr.sh` keep passing; the `321|ready` case still skips).
- A draft continued by a different runner than its author is accepted by Layer 6.

## Verification

Extend `test-pulse-issue-reconcile-stale-open-pr.sh` with draft-checkpoint cases (stale → reset; live lease → skip; local continuation process → skip). After deploy, confirm #35977 and #36061 leave `status:in-progress` via `stale_assignment_reset` and that pulse.log shows `PR_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_DISPATCHED` or one `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` for #35984/#36070.

</details>

title: t18825: perf(gh-api): label same-login other-device REST-core residual in quota series (t18804 follow-up)
body:
## Task


Label the REST-core residual that comes from **other runner devices authenticated as the same GitHub login** as `same_login_external_cost` in the quota report. It must not be shown as "unexplained" local consumption. Follow-up to #36054 (t18804). It needs the series metadata from PR #36182 (credential digest, reset epoch and `used` on default governor rows).

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Label the REST-core residual that comes from **other runner devices authenticated as the same GitHub login** as `same_login_external_cost` in the quota report. It must not be shown as "unexplained" local consumption. Follow-up to #36054 (t18804). It needs the series metadata from PR #36182 (credential digest, reset epoch and `used` on default governor rows).

## Why (evidence from a live window, 2026-10-31T02:52:42Z–02:59:32Z, one reset epoch)

- A read-only sampler polled `GET /rate_limit` (free) every ~2 s for the host default credential (digest prefix `2c37be71b4fc`, reset `1793415577`). The `used` counter went up by **413**. This host's `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` holds **131** matching rest-core attempt costs. The residual is **282 (68.3%)**. An earlier 254 s window showed 85.1% (188/221).
- Coverage on this host is close to complete. The sampler saw 694 native `gh` children under `gh-transport-governor.py`, against 733 logged governor rows. The only same-OS-user native `gh` processes that bypass the shim were 12 `gh send-telemetry` (no REST cost), 1 `gh api user` from the opencode runtime and 1 `gh auth git-credential`. Local unlogged calls cannot explain 282 units.
- Runner devices in the dispatch claims show **two active devices for the login `alex-solovyev`**: `device-1783824075-…` (this host) and `device-1791380361-…` (not on this host; no `device-id` file under this host's HOME matches it). The second device posted an ops comment on #36174 at 02:56:02Z, inside the window. GitHub REST-core limits are per user, so both devices draw from the same 5000/h bucket. Only this host's consumption reaches this host's log.
- The other OS user on this host runs as a different login (`vladimirdulov`, devices `device-1783824570-…` and `device-1791387943-…`). Its claims and comments are authored by that login, so it uses a separate quota bucket. It is not counted as a consumer of this credential.

Result: the majority of the "unexplained" share in this window is most consistent with the second same-login device. This is an inference from the device inventory plus a concurrent write. Proof needs that device's own log for the same (digest, reset) window.

## How

1. In the rest-core series output (`.agents/scripts/gh-api-aggregate.awk`: `collect_quota` / `emit_quota_minutes`), compute `external_cost = max(used_delta - local_attempt_cost, 0)` for each (credential digest, reset) series, using consecutive response-owned `used` values. Report it as `same_login_external_cost`. Keep it separate from `residual` and from `same_credential_reset_unknown_cost`; never subtract it from anything.
2. Annotate the report with the active runner devices for the credential's login when that list is available without extra API calls (for example, the dispatch-claim/ledger state already kept by `.agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh` or `dispatch-claim-helper.sh`). If no local source exists, print `other_devices: unknown` instead of making extra requests. These paths are provisional; confirm the cheapest local source first.
3. Optional: document how to confirm the attribution. Run the same sampler window on both devices and compare (digest, reset, `used`) series.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-api-aggregate.awk`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`

## File notes

The aggregate holds the series/minute output; the instrument script handles report rendering, if a field label is needed. Extend the existing quota-series test assertions near the `same_credential_reset_unknown_cost` cases. The device-inventory source is provisional (see How step 2).

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: a synthetic series whose `used` delta is larger than the local cost reports the difference as `same_login_external_cost`, and `residual` is unchanged.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the touched shell files.
- Live: after PR #36182 is deployed, a 5–10 minute window on the host shows `same_login_external_cost` close to the sampler residual.

## Acceptance

- The report separates local unlogged cost from cost by other devices on the same login, within one credential and reset series.
- No new GitHub API calls are added to the report path.

title: setup: skip bundled Chromium on Playwright pin-bump reinstall when AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE is valid
body:
## What

After a Playwright pin bump, setup should not re-download bundled Chromium when `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE` points to a valid executable file.

## Why

Follow-up to #36181 / PR #36188. Since that PR, `runtime-check` accepts a valid configured executable in place of bundled Chromium, so in the steady state setup skips the install. When `PINNED_VERSION` in `.agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs` changes, `installedVersion !== version` and readiness fails, as intended, because the package must update. Setup then runs `playwright-runtime.mjs install chromium firefox webkit` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`, `_setup_browser_tools_playwright`). That downloads the bundled Chromium build the operator retired, once per pin bump.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh` `_setup_browser_tools_playwright`: on the not-ready path, read `configuredExecutable` from the `runtime-check` JSON. The previous commit already captures the output in `runtime_status`. When it is non-null, run `install firefox webkit` instead of `install chromium firefox webkit`, and print why.
- Keep `playwright-runtime.mjs install` itself unchanged: explicit callers keep their browser list. Default `install` with no args still means `chromium`.
- Pattern: the `runtime_status` capture and the `configuredExecutable` check added in PR #36188 in the same function.

### Files Scope

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`

## Acceptance

1. Valid `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE` and a stale pin (`AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION` differs from the installed version): non-interactive setup invokes `install firefox webkit` only.
2. Variable unset or invalid: unchanged (`install chromium firefox webkit`).

## Verification

- Use the stubbed-`node` setup driver approach from PR #36188's testing notes: source `setup/_common.sh` and `setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`, set `NON_INTERACTIVE=true`, and use a `node` shim that echoes `install` args. Assert the browser list for both cases.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`.

Tier: `tier:simple` candidate. One function, pattern already present in the file.

title: t18826: fix(gh-shim): answer gh api user from GraphQL viewer when REST core is deferred or in cooldown
body:
## Task


When REST core is in cooldown or the transport governor defers a read, every `gh api user` identity lookup (about 90 call sites under `.agents/scripts/`) fails, even though GraphQL quota is plentiful. Callers fail closed, so lifecycle steps (claim release, PR creation, claims, dedup, merge gates) stop or silently skip. Fix it once in the `gh` shim: answer `gh api user` from the live GraphQL `viewer` when the REST attempt is deferred or blocked by local cooldown.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When REST core is in cooldown or the transport governor defers a read, every `gh api user` identity lookup (about 90 call sites under `.agents/scripts/`) fails, even though GraphQL quota is plentiful. Callers fail closed, so lifecycle steps (claim release, PR creation, claims, dedup, merge gates) stop or silently skip. Fix it once in the `gh` shim: answer `gh api user` from the live GraphQL `viewer` when the REST attempt is deferred or blocked by local cooldown.

## Why

This class keeps coming back and has been patched one call site at a time:

- #36036 (closed): `interactive-session-helper.sh` claim silently skipped when REST core was exhausted; fixed locally with a GraphQL viewer fallback (`_isc_current_user`).
- #36184: `shared-repo-state-guard.sh` read a deferred `gh api user` as "not managed", dropping a worker's `CLAIM_RELEASED` and stranding #35977 / draft #35984; fixed locally in the same way.
- 2026-10-31T03:1xZ: `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` for PR #36191 failed three times with `Open-PR linkage evidence is unavailable or ambiguous`. `issue-open-pr-guard.sh` `issue_open_pr_guard_check` calls `gh api user --jq '.login // empty'`, which printed `[gh-cooldown] primary-core active=true retry_at=1793418491; unrelated API resources remain available`. The GraphQL `gh pr list` in the same guard succeeded.

Budget evidence at the same time: `gh api rate_limit` showed core `102/5000` and graphql `4917/5000`. A 1h `gh-api-instrument.sh report` showed `rest-core min_remaining=0` and `graphql min_remaining=3351`. REST core runs out every hour while GraphQL stays mostly idle, so REST-only identity reads are the weak link.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/gh` — in the conservative direct REST GET fast path (`_SHIM_PLAIN_READ`, the `api <endpoint>` / `api <endpoint> --jq EXPR` shape), special-case endpoint `user` (and `/user`). Run the REST transport first, unchanged. If it returns 75 (governor `local_admission` deferral) or is refused by the local primary-core cooldown before any HTTP attempt, call `gh api graphql -f query='query{viewer{login databaseId name}}'`. Synthesize `{"login":…,"id":…,"name":…}` and apply the caller's `--jq`/`-q` expression with `jq -r`. If the expression references fields other than `login`, `id` or `name`, keep the original failure; never invent fields. Record the decision with `gh_record_call` (for example route decision `identity-graphql-fallback`).
- Trust boundary (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`): the answer is a live read with the same credential and is never cached (keep the no-cache rule in `shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` `_gh_current_user_allows_repo_write`). Validate the login against `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*(\[bot\])?$`; on malformed output keep the original failure exit code.
- Do not fall back on an HTTP verdict (401/403/404 from REST); only no-attempt deferral/cooldown qualifies.
- Reference patterns: `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` `_dsi_resolve_runner_login`, `shared-repo-state-guard.sh` `_aidevops_repo_state_graphql_viewer` (GH#36184), `interactive-session-helper.sh` `_isc_current_user` (#36036). Governor deferral is in `gh-transport-controls.sh` `_gh_transport_run_rest` (rc 75, `deferred_by=local_admission`). `gh_native_response.py` `_request_resource` already routes `graphql` outside REST admission.
- Once the shim covers it, the per-site fallbacks can stay; they are harmless redundancy.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-controls.sh`

title: t18827: fix(gh): pace REST admissions as time-to-reset divided by remaining quota
body:
## Task


Pace governed GitHub REST admissions evenly over the observed quota window:
spacing between admissions = time remaining until `x-ratelimit-reset` divided
by the remaining allowance (`x-ratelimit-remaining` minus local in-flight
reservations), with a small burst tolerance so parallel reads do not serialize.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py` `primary_wait()`: replace
  the healthy exemption and demand estimate with a GCRA-style next-slot
  schedule persisted in the existing `pacing` table (`retry_at` = next slot).
  interval = (reset - now) / available; admit when next slot - burst
  tolerance <= now; then advance the slot by one interval. Reset the schedule
  on a new window or increased remaining. Keep the final-point and stale-refresh
  exemptions and the secondary ceilings.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`: update the pacing
  tests that encoded the healthy exemption to the new semantics.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## What

Pace governed GitHub REST admissions evenly over the observed quota window:
spacing between admissions = time remaining until `x-ratelimit-reset` divided
by the remaining allowance (`x-ratelimit-remaining` minus local in-flight
reservations), with a small burst tolerance so parallel reads do not serialize.

## Why (observed evidence, 2026-10-31)

- REST core (`gh-pat`, one credential fingerprint) reached 0/5,000 in the
  window ending 02:48:10Z; `gh pr review-handoff` and release merges were
  deferred until reset.
- Local attempt log (`~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log`) for that drain:
  1,147 governed rest-core attempts. Top callers: pulse-wrapper.sh 362,
  pulse-merge-routine.sh 252, full-loop-helper.sh 194, gh-checks-wait-helper.sh
  105, review-bot-gate-helper.sh 75. The server consumed about 5,000 points in
  the same window, so most spend was not governed or logged as attempts.
- In the next window, `gh api rate_limit` showed 4,415 used about 24 minutes
  after reset, then 4,998 used about 3 minutes later. The local log recorded only
  about 45 governed rest-core attempts during those 3 minutes. Live ungoverned
  consumers included `gh pr checks --watch --interval 60` and `gh run watch
  --interval 30`. Their opaque native commands bypass the governor
  (`.agents/scripts/gh-transport-controls.sh` `_gh_transport_run_rest`
  accepts only supported `gh api` GETs). Exact per-consumer attribution of the
  remaining spend is not proven.
- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py` `primary_wait()` skips pacing while
  more than half of the observed quota is available (`healthy`). Below half, it
  paces only when 60-second demand would exhaust the window. Bursts can
  therefore spend 2,500+ points unpaced. Pacing on server-reported
  `remaining` also absorbs ungoverned spend, because the header reflects all
  consumers of the credential.

## Acceptance

- At 5,000 remaining and 3,600 s to reset, sustained admission is limited to
  about 1 per 0.72 s after a burst of at most 10.
- Near exhaustion (for example 100 remaining, 1,000 s left), admissions are
  spaced about 10 s apart.
- Existing secondary-ceiling, cooldown, last-point and revalidation tests pass.

## Verification

`python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`;
`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim-transport-cases.sh`; observe
`gh api rate_limit` after release to confirm quota is not exhausted early.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

Opaque long-running pollers (`gh pr checks --watch`, `gh run watch`) bypass
the governor. Route them through governed polling, or count their spend.

title: t18828: fix(worktree): fresh archive-verification slots stay unregistered and guard hides identity-changed reason (post GH#36103)
body:
## Task


After GH#36103 (PR #36107, shipped in v3.39.99), `worktree-helper.sh remove` still cannot finish for some archived worktrees on macOS. Two failure modes remain:

1. **Fresh verification slots are created unregistered.** A new archive-verification attempt on v3.39.99 leaves a `.restore-*` slot holding a Git-registered, clean, detached worktree with **no** `worktree_owners` row, **no** `worktree_creation_backends` row, **no** `worktree_managed_lifetimes` row and no `.creation.json`. The journal stays `canonical_restore.state: "restoring"`. `recover_unsealed` requires a legacy creation record, so the next attempt fails again with `restore-proof:unsealed-copy-retained; inspect owned scratch`. Each attempt can strand a new slot.
2. **The removal guard refuses with an empty user-facing reason.** `worktree-helper-cmds.sh` prints `Reason: guard-refused`, but `~/.aidevops/logs/cleanup_worktrees.log` records `git-worktree-identity-changed` for the same path (`recovery_path=archive-first`). The source worktree is unlocked, has no owner row and no process cwd.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

After GH#36103 (PR #36107, shipped in v3.39.99), `worktree-helper.sh remove` still cannot finish for some archived worktrees on macOS. Two failure modes remain:

1. **Fresh verification slots are created unregistered.** A new archive-verification attempt on v3.39.99 leaves a `.restore-*` slot holding a Git-registered, clean, detached worktree with **no** `worktree_owners` row, **no** `worktree_creation_backends` row, **no** `worktree_managed_lifetimes` row and no `.creation.json`. The journal stays `canonical_restore.state: "restoring"`. `recover_unsealed` requires a legacy creation record, so the next attempt fails again with `restore-proof:unsealed-copy-retained; inspect owned scratch`. Each attempt can strand a new slot.
2. **The removal guard refuses with an empty user-facing reason.** `worktree-helper-cmds.sh` prints `Reason: guard-refused`, but `~/.aidevops/logs/cleanup_worktrees.log` records `git-worktree-identity-changed` for the same path (`recovery_path=archive-first`). The source worktree is unlocked, has no owner row and no process cwd.

## Why

Evidence, 2026-10-31, v3.39.99, removing 8 superseded badge-sync worktrees from one managed repo (content already merged to the default branch):

- 5 of 8 removed successfully (`worktree-removed ... mode=trash recovery_path=archive-first`). So PR #36107 reclaimed the old pre-fix slots.
- 2 remaining transactions now point at slots created 04:49–04:51 UTC today by v3.39.99, with zero rows in all three registry tables and no `.creation.json`. `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all --ignored` is empty, no `S`/lowercase `ls-files -v` flags, and HEAD is contained in 13 refs. So the content is safe, but it is unprovable under the current rules.
- 1 remaining transaction has an older (29 Oct) slot that **does** satisfy the #36107 rules (legacy row present, no owner, clean, reachable). Removal still stops at the guard (`guard-refused` shown; log shows `git-worktree-identity-changed` for a sibling attempt).
- No open issue covers this; prior fixes: #35964 (GH#35957), #36107 (GH#36103).

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` creation path (`creation_receipt` and its caller), find why creation stops after `git worktree add` but before any registry row or `.creation.json` is written on Darwin/legacy-guards. Write the creation record before or atomically with `git worktree add`, so an interrupted attempt is always recoverable. Surface the original exception instead of the later `unsealed-copy-retained`.
2. Extend `recover_unsealed` to reclaim a slot with **no** registration rows only when every other check from #36107 holds (slot inode match, sole entry `worktree`, Git registration in the same common dir, clean including ignored files, no hidden index flags, HEAD ref-reachable). Fail closed otherwise.
3. In `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh` `_remove_validate_path` / `_remove_show_guard_error`, propagate `WORKTREE_REMOVAL_GUARD_REASON` so `git-worktree-identity-changed` is printed with its recovery text instead of `guard-refused`. Investigate why the source identity is judged changed after an archive-first attempt; if a verification copy changes the admin-dir numbering or identity inputs, bind identity to stable fields.

Never delete `.producer-archives` content; only verification scratch.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_registration.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fixture: creation interrupted after `git worktree add` leaves a recoverable record, and the next `remove` reaches a fresh sealed proof.
- Fixture: an unsealed slot with no registration rows but otherwise clean/reachable/same-common-dir is reclaimed; dirty, ignored-file, hidden-index, unreachable-HEAD or foreign-common-dir variants still fail closed.
- A guard refusal prints the specific reason recorded in `cleanup_worktrees.log`, never bare `guard-refused` when a reason exists.
- On the reporting machine, the 3 remaining worktrees remove via `worktree-helper.sh remove` with no manual scratch deletion.

title: t18830: fix(dispatch): bound pre-launch abort loops fleet-wide with a self-healing windowed backoff
body:
## Task


Pre-launch dispatch aborts loop forever across runners, leave one reason-less `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=prelaunch` comment per attempt, and the zero-attempt fuse never sees them. Make that evidence visible fleet-wide and replace the permanent `status:blocked` fuse with a self-healing, windowed backoff that runs before any claim is posted.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Pre-launch dispatch aborts loop forever across runners, leave one reason-less `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=prelaunch` comment per attempt, and the zero-attempt fuse never sees them. Make that evidence visible fleet-wide and replace the permanent `status:blocked` fuse with a self-healing, windowed backoff that runs before any claim is posted.

## Why

Observed on #36061 (2026-10-31 04:46–05:43Z): two peer runners alternated five dispatch attempts, about 25 minutes apart. Each left a `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=prelaunch` comment with no `DISPATCH_CLAIM` and no `ready`. Nothing stopped the loop, and the thread gained a new ops comment every cycle.

Root causes (code evidence):

1. `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` `_dlw_begin_prelaunch` posts a public prelaunch lease renewal (GH#34057) before worktree/runtime preparation. On a later pre-runtime failure, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` `_release_dispatch_claim_on_abort` deletes the `DISPATCH_CLAIM` (t3549) but leaves the lease, which was added after t3549.
2. `pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh` `_dlw_comment_bloat_metrics_from_json` counts zero-attempt evidence only as unmatched `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comments. Deleting the claim erases the evidence, so `_dlw_hold_repeated_zero_output` never trips.
3. The same metrics trust only OWNER/MEMBER (GH#32928). On a User-owned repo every peer runner is `COLLABORATOR`, so the fuse ignores every peer runner's failures even when claims survive.
4. When the fuse does trip, it sets `status:blocked` with no automatic release (#35407 stayed blocked for about 14h until an interactive session took it). That conflicts with the rule that evidence-less or transient blocks stay dispatchable.

## How

- `pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`:
  - Count an orphan prelaunch lease as zero-attempt evidence when all of these hold: trusted author; lease token, device and session present; older than `DISPATCH_CLAIM_ORPHAN_GRACE`; no surviving `DISPATCH_CLAIM` with that lease token; no same-author `ready`/`terminal` lease for the token. Deduplicate per author+token.
  - Resolve ambiguous-association authors (COLLABORATOR/CONTRIBUTOR/NONE) of dispatch-evidence-shaped comments with `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority` (`shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`). Only write/maintain/admin counts, and a lookup failure fails closed (#aidevops:trust-boundary). Reset and approval authority stay OWNER/MEMBER only.
  - Emit two extra TSV columns: zero evidence within `ZERO_OUTPUT_HOLD_WINDOW_SECONDS` (default 43200) and whether a trusted hold notice already exists in that window.
  - `_dlw_hold_repeated_zero_output`: hold while the windowed count is at or above the threshold. Do not change labels. Post at most one notice per window. Dispatch resumes automatically as evidence ages out.
- `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` `dispatch_with_dedup`: evaluate the hold before the dedup/claim layers and return a benign block (rc 3, `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=zero_attempt_backoff`), so held attempts post no claim and no lease.
- `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`: reuse the pre-claim metrics for prompt preparation and drop the post-lease hold call.

- Orphan prelaunch leases from a trusted runner count as zero-attempt evidence, once per lease token.
- A write-permission COLLABORATOR runner's unmatched claims and orphan leases count. A read or triage collaborator, or a failed lookup, does not.
- Evidence older than the window does not hold dispatch. The hold changes no labels and posts at most one notice per window.
- A held issue posts no `DISPATCH_CLAIM` or `DISPATCH_LEASE`.

title: Archive verification local base import times out and blocks guarded worktree removal
body:
## Observed failure

An explicitly authorized archive-first cleanup canary passed sealed lifetime proof, clean Git status and HEAD-in-default-branch checks. The supported removal helper then stopped with `producer:evidence-unavailable`. The source remained present and clean; the other eleven approved candidates were not attempted.

A separate archive verify invocation exposed `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` after 60 seconds in `worktree_archive_snapshot.seed_base`, called by `worktree_archive_objects.verify_object_graph` / `verify_git_objects`. The timed-out argv was `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -C <verification-scratch> -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null fetch --quiet --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head <local-common-dir> <recorded-base-sha>`.

Private source names, paths, commit IDs and archive receipts are intentionally omitted. This is a local object import, not an observed network-authentication failure. The relative cost of the Git shim, object packing, host contention and other Git work remains unprofiled.

## Files Scope and reference pattern

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_snapshot.py`: `seed_base` around lines 69-80.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_git.py`: `git` helper around lines 14-25, currently an unconditional `timeout=60`.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_producer.py`: `failure_reason` and `check`; distinguish actionable timeout evidence from opaque `producer:evidence-unavailable` without exposing raw diagnostics.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py` and existing producer failure-classification cases under `.agents/scripts/tests/worktree_recovery_producer_cases.py` only as needed.
- READ `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_objects.py` and `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py` for independent verification and restoration contracts.

## Requested implementation

Profile and reproduce the bounded local base-import failure using disposable repositories and existing test tooling. Repair the responsible import/budget path with bounded resource-aware behavior; do not merely raise every Git timeout or bypass the installed Git policy shim.

Preserve exact-base validation, independently verified restoration, process ownership, archival receipts, source identity, cancellation cleanup and fail-closed removal. Keep source repositories read-only during verification. A timeout must retain source and archive and produce a sanitized actionable reason.

Do not delete transaction journals or scratch to force retries, increase dispatch caps, weaken process guards, stop sessions or remove production worktrees.

## Verification and acceptance

Use existing archive-lifecycle and producer regression runners with focused cases for slow/failed local imports, successful retry through the supported transaction path, and retained source/archive on timeout. Run existing Python compatibility checks and `git diff --check` for changed files.

Do not claim the incident recovered from a merged PR or unit-test exit alone: actual guarded canary removal and independently verified recovery receipts require separately authorized operational validation. This issue authorizes code repair in disposable fixtures, not production deletion.

Related merged restore-slot repair: PR #36107. Rollout parent #35359 is not acceptance of this failure. Open searches for `seed_base` and archive/fetch/timeout found no matching open implementation issue.

title: t18832: fix(pulse-merge): skip partial parent closeout for planning publication PRs
body:
## Task


Skip the post-merge "Partial Parent Closeout" comment when the merged PR is a planning publication (body carries `<!-- aidevops:planning-publication:v1 ... -->`). Planning PRs only publish `TODO.md`/`todo/` entries and use `For #NNN` so they do not close the task they announce; they deliver no task scope.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Origin

Interactive fleet-health review (session objective: stop excessive automated comments on stale issues). Evidence: issue #36227 received a misleading "Partial Parent Closeout" comment after planning-only PR #36229 merged.

## What

Skip the post-merge "Partial Parent Closeout" comment when the merged PR is a planning publication (body carries `<!-- aidevops:planning-publication:v1 ... -->`). Planning PRs only publish `TODO.md`/`todo/` entries and use `For #NNN` so they do not close the task they announce; they deliver no task scope.

## Why

`shared-todo-commit.sh` (`_todo_planning_pr_body`, around `:410-439`) writes `- For #NNN` for every task in a planning PR. On merge, `_pm_handle_partial_parent_closeout` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-issue-closeout.sh:125-182`) treats that reference as a parent delivery. `_pm_issue_needs_partial_closeout` (`:73-93`) classifies nearly every worker-ready brief as a "broad parent", because briefs contain an `Acceptance Criteria` heading and 2+ checklist items. The result is a comment on a fresh leaf task that claims "PR #N merged against this broad parent", repeats the task's own acceptance criteria as "follow-ups", and copies the interactive session's cost signature from the planning PR body.

GitHub search on 2026-10-31 found 45 issues carrying a "Partial Parent Closeout" comment generated from a planning publication PR, out of 148 partial closeouts overall.

## Tier

`tier:simple`: one guard in one function, plus one regression case in the existing suite.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-issue-closeout.sh`: in `_pm_extract_partial_parent_reference` (`:56-65`), return an empty reference when the PR body contains `aidevops:planning-publication:v1`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-parent-closeout.sh`: add one case: a planning publication body with `- For #23932` and a brief-shaped issue body posts no comment and makes no issue fetch.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_handle_post_merge_actions` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:1072`) is the only caller. Test stubs in `test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-post-merge-label-fetch.sh` and `test-pulse-merge-parent-task-close-guard.sh` replace the function and are unaffected.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** removes one GitHub issue-comment write for planning PRs. No label or state changes.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-pulse-merge-partial-parent-closeout.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** reads the existing planning publication marker written by `shared-todo-commit.sh`; marker format unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed by `setup.sh` on the normal update path.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. Existing comments stay as historical records.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the guard.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add the marker guard after the PR body fetch in `_pm_extract_partial_parent_reference`; keep `return 0` semantics.
2. Add the regression case and run the verification below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** read-only guard; no new writes.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older runners keep posting until updated; the PR-number dedup marker still prevents duplicates.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged.

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-parent-closeout.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-issue-closeout.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-parent-closeout.sh

title: t18833: fix(terminal-blocker): re-arm permission_required holds that have no publishe...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18833` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(terminal-blocker): re-arm permission_required holds that have no published permission request

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Origin

Interactive fleet-health review on 2026-10-31 (session objective: Pulse and workers continually resolve what they can; humans receive only needs they can act on). Maintainer decision recorded in that session: evidence-less blocked exits stay dispatchable.

## What

A `permission_required` terminal-blocker hold with no published, actionable permission request must not be a permanent human-gated hold. Re-arm it under a bounded, windowed backoff through the existing terminal-blocker recovery path. Keep the hold when a real request exists (`needs-maintainer-permissions` label or a `worker-permission-helper.sh` request marker without a later approval).

## Why

`permission_required` is a retry-only class (`_TBC_RETRY_ONLY_REARM_REASONS`, `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:39`). Its first observation projects `status:blocked`, and only an OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` line re-arms it (`terminal_blocker_observation_hold_active`, `:606-635`; recovery `_tbr_release_circuit_hold`, `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:717-799`).

The public release says only "Resolve the evidenced permission prerequisite". The evidence stays in the releasing runner's protected telemetry. Unless the worker also ran `worker-permission-helper.sh request` (which posts "Maintainer permission required" with a request ID and capability list, and adds `needs-maintainer-permissions`), the maintainer has nothing to approve.

GH#36033 showed that many of these releases are runner-local faults: one device released six different issues as `permission_required` within 15 minutes. That fix stops new storms. It does not release the backlog.

GraphQL search on 2026-10-31 for open `status:blocked` issues with a `reason=permission_required` release:

- 37 in one managed private organisation, of which only 3 have a visible permission request. Releases came from three runners, dated 2026-09-11 to 2026-10-30, six of them on the GH#36033 incident day.
- 2 in a second managed organisation.
- 4 in personal repositories, for example #35850 (released 11 minutes after dispatch on 2026-10-28, OpenCode 1.19.4, no request posted). #35592 is the counter-example: a real request `perm-f288b40c03806601` with `needs-maintainer-permissions`, which must stay held.

## Tier

`tier:thinking`: changes a trust-sensitive hold predicate (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`), shared by the dispatch gate and the recovery helper.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: add `terminal_blocker_permission_request_evidenced <comments_json> <issue_json>`. It returns 0 when the issue carries `needs-maintainer-permissions`, or an authoritative comment contains the `worker-permission-helper.sh` request marker (`PERMISSION_REQUEST_MARKER`) with no later approval/retry. In `terminal_blocker_observation_hold_active` (`:627-630`), keep holding `permission_required` only when it is evidenced, or when the newest observation is inside the backoff window. Otherwise return 1 (re-armed).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: in `_tbr_release_circuit_hold` (`:770-785`), add decision `unevidenced_permission_window` for `permission_required` evidence that is not evidenced and older than the window. Project `status:available` through `_tbr_project_rearm` with the existing hidden receipt, binding the observation id and window index in the receipt key so each window releases at most once. Also confirm `_tbr_circuit_blocks_release` (`:655-672`) does not re-hold it.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` (it also covers `_tbr_release_circuit_hold`): add the cases in Acceptance Criteria.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`: add one short paragraph next to the zero-attempt backoff contract.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** dispatch reads hold state through `terminal_blocker_circuit_active` / `terminal_blocker_observation_hold_active` (callers: `rg -n "terminal_blocker_observation_hold_active|terminal_blocker_circuit_active" .agents/scripts --glob '!tests/**'`). The recovery helper intake seeds from `label:"status:blocked" "Terminal blocker" in:comments` (`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:306-311`, `:419`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the only new write is the existing `set_issue_status available` plus the hidden `aidevops:terminal-blocker-rearmed` receipt in `_tbr_project_rearm` (`:802-827`). No new visible comments, which avoids comment storms.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` (circuit and recovery helper), `test-permission-block-breaker.sh` (GH#36033 runner breaker must stay effective).
- **Schemas/config:** the window constant mirrors `ZERO_OUTPUT_HOLD_WINDOW_SECONDS=43200` (12h) from the zero-attempt backoff (GH#36214). Reuse or co-locate it; do not add a user config key unless needed.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed by `setup.sh` on the normal update path.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. Existing holds are picked up by recovery intake on the next pass.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the predicate. Posted receipts are inert hidden markers.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Trust boundary:** re-arming schedules a new attempt only; it never grants a permission. A worker that hits a real guard again must go through `worker-permission-helper.sh request`, which publishes an actionable request and is then held as evidenced. Mark new predicates `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
- **Storm safety:** the GH#36033 runner-local breaker plus the window bound attempts to about 2 per issue per day. Never re-arm while `needs-maintainer-permissions`, `hold-for-review`, `no-auto-dispatch`, `parent-task` or another hold label is present (existing guard in `_tbr_release_circuit_hold:724-730`).
- **Mixed versions:** older runners keep holding; newer runners release once per window via the receipt key.
- **Idempotency:** the receipt key includes observation id + window index.

### Verification Before Dispatch
